title: 60 SQL Practice Queries with Answers: PostgreSQL
summary: Sixty graded SQL drills on PostgreSQL 16 over one small employees/departments/orders dataset. They run from basics and filtering through aggregates, joins, subqueries, window functions and CTEs to classic interview scenarios. Every task has its solution and the result it returns on the sample rows.

chapters.title: 60 SQL Practice Queries: PostgreSQL Drills
points: Nine task families, ordered from basic to advanced: basics, filtering, expressions, aggregates, joins, subqueries, window functions, CTEs, interview scenarios
Every task is an instruction with a solution that runs on PostgreSQL 16 and the result it returns on the shared sample data
One dataset throughout: employees, departments and orders, with the full sample rows on the next page

chapters.title: The Sample Schema and Data
points: departments(id, name, location): 5 rows. Engineering/Austin, Sales/Chicago, HR/Boston, Marketing/Chicago and Legal/Denver; Legal has no employees
employees(id, name, salary, dept_id, manager_id, hire_date): 8 rows. Asha has no manager and Gus has no department; Ben and Chen tie at 120000
orders(id, employee_id, customer, amount, order_date): 8 rows from Jan to Mar 2024. Orders 1 and 2 are exact duplicates, and employees 1, 2, 3 and 6 have no orders

chapters.title: Basics: SELECT, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT
points: Select every column and row from departments
Select only the name and salary of every employee
List the distinct locations in departments
List employees by salary, highest first, breaking ties by name
Return the 3 highest-paid employees with LIMIT
Show each employee's name and annual pay as salary * 12, using the alias annual_pay

chapters.title: Filtering: WHERE, AND/OR, IN, BETWEEN, LIKE, NULL
points: Find employees earning more than 100000
Find Engineering employees (dept_id 1) earning at least 120000, using AND
Find employees in departments 2 or 3 using IN
Find employees earning between 80000 and 100000 inclusive using BETWEEN
Find employees whose name contains the letter 'e' regardless of case, using ILIKE
Find employees with no department using IS NULL
Find orders placed in February 2024 with a half-open date range, not BETWEEN

chapters.title: Expressions: CASE, COALESCE, Strings, Dates
points: Label each employee's pay band as High (100000 or more), Mid (80000 to 99999) or Low with CASE

chapters.title: Aggregates: GROUP BY and HAVING
points: Compare COUNT(*) with COUNT(dept_id) on employees to see how NULL is treated
Return the sum, average, minimum and maximum employee salary in one query
Count employees per department_id with GROUP BY
Compute the average salary per department, rounded to 2 decimals
Keep only departments with at least 2 employees using HAVING
Total the order amount per customer, largest first
Show the order count and total amount per month, keeping months with a total above 2000

chapters.title: Joins: INNER, LEFT, Anti-Join, Self-Join
points: List each employee with their department name using INNER JOIN
List all employees, including Gus with no department, using LEFT JOIN
Find departments with no employees (Legal) using LEFT JOIN ... IS NULL
Find employees who have placed no orders using an anti-join
Total the order amount per employee name by joining employees to orders and grouping
List each employee with their manager's name using a self-join
Find employees who earn more than their manager

chapters.title: Subqueries: Scalar, IN, EXISTS, Correlated
points: Find employees earning more than the company average salary using a scalar subquery
Find employees who work in a Chicago department using IN (SELECT ...)
Find departments that have at least one employee using EXISTS
Find employees with no orders using NOT EXISTS
Find employees who manage nobody using NOT IN, filtering NULL manager_id so the result is not empty
Find employees earning more than their own department's average with a correlated subquery
Find each department's highest salary through a subquery in FROM, then join back to name the employee

chapters.title: Window Functions: Ranking, Running Totals, LAG
points: Number employees by salary descending with ROW_NUMBER
Show RANK and DENSE_RANK side by side on salary, where Ben and Chen tie
Rank employees by salary inside each department with PARTITION BY
Compute a running total of order amount by order date and id
Show each order's amount next to the same customer's previous order amount with LAG

chapters.title: CTEs: WITH, Chained and Recursive

Chain two CTEs: per-customer totals, then customers above the average total

chapters.title: Interview Scenarios: Nth Highest, Duplicates, Trends

Find the Nth highest distinct salary with DISTINCT, ORDER BY and OFFSET N-1

Show each month's order total and its change from the previous month with LAG

chapters.title: SQL Drills Cheatsheet
points: Logical execution order: FROM/JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT/window, DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT
Join picker: INNER keeps matches only, LEFT keeps all left rows, LEFT + IS NULL is the anti-join, a self-join relates a table to itself
Ranking picker: ROW_NUMBER is always unique, RANK leaves gaps after ties, DENSE_RANK has no gaps
NULL traps: = NULL never matches (use IS NULL), COUNT(col) skips NULLs, NOT IN with a NULL in the list returns nothing, WHERE cannot filter aggregates (use HAVING)
